summary: Edmund Ronald Leach studied at Clare College, Cambridge, King's College, Cambridge, and the London School of Economics (PhD 1947). He was a lecturer at LSE (1947–1953) and held Cambridge posts as Professor (1953–1978) and King's College Provost (1966–1979).

Working in religious studies and psychology, Edo Shonin is attested in 2015 as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Linguist Eduard Böhmer studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from ~1847 to 1851. He held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and at the University of Strasbourg (~1872–1879).

Sinologist Eduard Erkes studied at the University of Leipzig (~1910–1913) under August Conrady. He held academic posts at Leipzig (~1917–1958), succeeding Conrady, and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1947–1951).

Eduard Hermann, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Jena under Berthold Delbrück. He taught at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and served as Professor at the University of Göttingen (1917–1937), succeeding Jacob Wackernagel.

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Eduard Müller-Hess completed an Inauguraldissertation at the University of Leipzig in 1874. He is attested as a professor at the University of Bern in 1897–1898.

Indologist and philosopher Eduard Röer studied at Jena, Königsberg under Johann Friedrich Herbart, and under Franz Bopp. He held a postdoctorate at Humboldt University (1833) and worked for the East India Company and The Asiatic Society.

Eduard Sachau studied under Brockhaus, Fleischer, and Nöldeke, earning doctorates at Halle (1867). He served as professor of Semitic philology at Vienna (1869), professor at Frederick William University Berlin (1876–1920), and director of Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1887).

Eduard Schwyzer was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who succeeded Adolf Kaegi in 1914. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1902–1927), the University of Bonn (~1927–1932), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1943).

Linguist Eduard Sievers studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Georg Curtius, August Leskien, and Friedrich Zarncke. He held professorships at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and the University of Leipzig (1892–1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Philosopher Edvard Westermarck studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881–1890). He later held academic appointments at the London School of Economics (~1904–1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918–1932).

Edward Albert Gait, a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at University College London (~1880–1882). In 1914, he founded the Bihar Research Society, serving as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick, who worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, studied at Merton College and Oxford (MA 1875). He held posts at East India Company College (1845) and the Foreign Office (~1860–1863).
Edward Burnett Tylor worked in religious studies and anthropology. After studying at Grove House School, he held academic posts at the University of Seville and the University of Oxford (~1883–1909).

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He held posts at Presidency University, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta, before serving as Professor at the University of Cambridge from 1867 to 1903.

Edward C. Dimock Jr. was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Yale and Harvard Divinity School (PhD 1959). He served at the University of Chicago (1966–1993) and presided over the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972–1986).

Edward Capps studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. Working in archaeology and history, he held posts at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale University (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).
Edward Clive Bayley was an Indologist and historian who studied at the East India Company College (Haileybury) between ~1840 and 1842. In 1842, he entered a post in the Indian Civil Service.

Edward Conze studied at Tübingen, Kiel, Heidelberg, Hamburg, Bonn, and Cologne under Max Walleser and Max Scheler. He held posts at the University of London, Wisconsin-Madison, Washington, UC Berkeley, and Lancaster University.
